result.description:
Concrete Support Services (CSS) is a fully independent concrete testing and engineering consultancy supporting construction projects right across Melbourne. From our laboratory and field operations, we deliver concrete testing, materials assessment and technical advice that builders, contractors and engineers rely on to keep their projects moving and compliant. Because we operate as a completely independent laboratory, our clients know that every result we issue is backed by integrity, confidentiality and impartiality. Our work aligns with Australian Standards and NATA requirements, and our team combines decades of hands-on concrete technology expertise with a genuine commitment to service. What sets us apart is speed paired with accuracy we understand that critical site activities can’t wait, so we go out of our way to turn around reliable field and laboratory results promptly and to consistently exceed what our clients expect. As we continue to grow, we’re looking for a motivated Civil Engineering Technician to join our team at Oakleigh South and play a hands-on role in delivering the quality and responsiveness our clients count on.

Key Responsibilities
•	Carry out and coordinate a full program of on-site and in-laboratory tests on concrete, construction materials and soils including sampling fresh concrete, casting and curing specimens, slump and compressive strength testing all in accordance with Australian Standards.
•	Interpret job briefs, project specifications and work assignment instructions, then apply the appropriate testing procedures and select the correct equipment for each task.
•	Record, collate and analyse test results, perform the associated computations, and enter data accurately and promptly into our laboratory data-management systems so clients receive fast, dependable results.
•	Prepare technical sketches, charts, tabulations and test reports that support civil engineering works such as roads, drainage, water supply and sewerage reticulation systems, dams and structural elements where concrete and materials testing is required.
•	Conduct site inspections of concrete and civil works, and help organise and oversee sampling, re-testing and remedial or maintenance verification where required.
•	Estimate material quantities and associated costs, and check that materials and finished works comply with specifications, regulations and relevant contract provisions.
•	Collect field data during site surveys and sampling runs including on road, pavement and infrastructure projects and consolidate it for analysis and reporting.
•	Calibrate, maintain and correctly operate field and laboratory testing equipment, and keep clear records of its condition and use.
•	Uphold the laboratory’s quality management system and safeguard the integrity, impartiality and confidentiality of every result, in line with NATA and Australian Standards requirements.
•	Liaise professionally with clients, site supervisors and project engineers, providing clear technical support and rapid feedback to accommodate critical site timelines.
•	Support concrete mix design and quality-control activities, contributing observations and data that help clients meet their construction project needs.
•	Follow all workplace health and safety procedures and contribute to a safe, well-organised working environment both on site and in the laboratory.

About You
•	Strong attention to detail and a methodical, accurate approach to testing and record-keeping.
•	Reliable, punctual and able to manage priorities to meet time-critical site demands.
•	A team player who communicates clearly and professionally with colleagues and clients.
•	Committed to integrity, impartiality and confidentiality in all aspects of the work.
•	Safety-conscious, with a genuine respect for standards, procedures and compliance.
•	Physically capable of the practical, hands-on aspects of field and laboratory testing.
•	Willing to learn, take direction and grow within a supportive, quality-driven team.

Qualifications & Experience
•	An AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in a relevant civil, engineering or materials-related discipline.
•	At least 1 year of relevant experience.

What We Offer
•	Salary:  $75,000 – $85,000 plus superannuation per annum.
•	Hours: Full-time position, typically 38 hours per week.
•	Location: Oakleigh South, VIC.

How to Apply
If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your resume together with a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience and qualifications.

Electrical Engineering Technician
Employer: Integra Switchboards Pty Ltd
Location: Brendale, Queensland 4500
Position: Full-time
Salary: AUD 80,000 to A$90,000 per annum plus superannuation, commensurate with skills and experience

Integra Switchboards Pty Ltd is seeking a skilled and experienced Electrical Engineering Technician to join their team in Brendale, Queensland. The successful candidate will support the design, manufacture, testing, commissioning and quality checking of low-voltage electrical switchboards, distribution boards, motor control centres and control panels.
This role is suited to a technically competent person with experience in electrical systems, switchboard manufacture, testing procedures, technical drawings, electrical components and Australian electrical standards.
Key duties and responsibilities
The Electrical Engineering Technician will be responsible for:
•	Assisting Electrical Engineers, project managers and senior technical staff with the design and layout of electrical switchboards, distribution boards, motor control centres, control panels, cabling arrangements and associated electrical systems.
•	Preparing, interpreting and reviewing technical drawings, wiring diagrams, layout drawings, schematics and electrical plans for switchboard manufacturing projects.
•	Conducting tests on electrical systems, components and switchboard assemblies to confirm operational performance, safety and compliance with project specifications.
•	Collecting technical data, recording test results, performing calculations, preparing test documentation, charts, reports and tabulations for engineering and quality assurance purposes.
•	Assisting with estimating material requirements, component quantities, labour requirements and project costs for switchboard and electrical assembly works.
•	Inspecting designs, manufactured switchboards and completed electrical assemblies to ensure compliance with specifications, Australian Standards, client requirements and safety requirements.
•	Assembling, installing, testing, calibrating, modifying and repairing electrical equipment, switchboard components, protection devices, metering equipment, indicating devices and control equipment.
•	Supporting workshop electrical functions, including installation of assemblies for protection relays, metering devices, control circuits and electrical indicating equipment.
•	Assisting with fault finding, technical problem solving and rectification of electrical issues during manufacture, testing and commissioning.
•	Liaising with internal design, fabrication, assembly and project teams to ensure switchboards are delivered accurately, safely and on time.
•	Maintaining accurate technical records, testing records, compliance documents and quality assurance documentation.
•	Ensuring all work is performed in accordance with workplace health and safety requirements, company procedures, project specifications and relevant Australian Standards.
Skills and experience required
Applicants must have:
•	Diploma or Bachelors in Electrical Engineering or related field
•	Atleast 2 years of experience in electrical switchboard manufacture, electrical systems, control panels, distribution boards, motor control centres or similar electrical engineering environments.
•	Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, schematics and technical specifications.
•	Experience conducting electrical tests, recording results and assisting with technical reporting.
•	Knowledge of electrical components such as circuit breakers, busbars, contactors, relays, metering equipment, control devices, terminals and cabling systems.
Skills Required
•	Good technical problem-solving skills and strong attention to detail.
•	Ability to work safely and effectively in a workshop/manufacturing environment.
•	Good communication skills and ability to work as part of a technical project team.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

About KRE8 IT
KRE8 IT is a Melbourne-based technology consulting company specialising in practical software delivery, low-code development, systems integration, and digital transformation. We work with clients to design, build, and support business-critical applications, with a strong focus on governed delivery, maintainable architecture, and high-quality outcomes.
We are seeking an OutSystems Developer / Consultant to support the design, development, implementation, and ongoing improvement of OutSystems applications for our clients.

About the role
The OutSystems Developer / Consultant will work across the full delivery lifecycle, including requirements analysis, solution design, application development, integration, testing, deployment support, and continuous improvement. The role requires strong hands-on OutSystems development capability as well as the ability to work in a consulting environment with clients and internal delivery teams.

Key responsibilities
*   Design, develop, test, and maintain applications using OutSystems.
*   Work with both OutSystems O11 and OutSystems Developer Cloud environments.
*   Translate business requirements into reliable, maintainable application solutions.
*   Develop integrations with external systems, APIs, data services, and business platforms.
*   Support implementation of complex business workflows, decision logic, and rules-driven functionality.
*   Collaborate with clients, stakeholders, designers, analysts, and other developers to deliver fit-for-purpose solutions.
*   Contribute to application architecture, technical design, estimation, documentation, and delivery planning.
*   Troubleshoot, optimise, and improve existing OutSystems applications.
*   Support quality assurance, deployment activities, and production support where required.
*   Apply secure, scalable, and maintainable development practices.

Required experience, qualifications, and skills
*   Minimum 1 year of experience developing applications with OutSystems, including both O11 and ODC.
*   A Bachelor’s degree or higher in a relevant field is required. Where the qualification is not directly relevant to the position, the applicant must demonstrate a minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience.
*   Must be based in Australia and able to work with clients operating under Australian regulatory requirements.
*   Strong software development experience, including application design, data modelling, integration, testing, and debugging.
*   Experience working in consulting, client delivery, or project-based software delivery environments.
*   Ability to analyse business requirements and convert them into practical technical solutions.
*   Strong communication skills and ability to work collaboratively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
*   Ability to work independently and manage delivery responsibilities with attention to quality and detail.

Highly regarded
*   Demonstrated experience implementing complex decision logic using business rules management systems.
*   Experience implementing applications in the healthcare industry.
*   Working understanding of the FHIR interoperability standard.
*   Experience with API integration, workflow automation, data exchange, and enterprise application integration.
*   Relevant OutSystems certifications.

How to apply
Please apply through this job advertisement platform with your resume and a short cover note outlining your relevant OutSystems experience, including your experience with O11 and ODC.

Full-time Electronics Engineer position available with a competitive salary. Join a growing telecommunications infrastructure company delivering advanced mobile coverage and wireless communication solutions across Australia, supporting complex commercial, infrastructure, and telecommunications projects.

3 Stand-out Bullet Points:
•	Full-Time Electronics Engineer
•	Salary from $80,000 to $90,000 p.a. plus superannuation
•	Position based in Kingsgrove NSW 2208

Position Overview
Digital Sydney Communications Pty Ltd specialises in mobile coverage solutions for telecommunications, commercial property, and infrastructure sectors. The company delivers Distributed Antenna Systems (DAS), In-Building Coverage solutions, outdoor network enhancements, and tower builds across complex commercial environments.

As the company expands nationally, operational delivery increasingly relies on advanced telecommunications and electronic systems managing RF performance, wireless coverage, network optimisation, testing, and operational reporting across multiple project sites. Skilled engineering capability is essential to maintaining network reliability, supporting project delivery, and ensuring scalable technical operations across the business.

We are seeking a full-time Electronics Engineer to support the design, testing, optimisation, commissioning, and maintenance of telecommunications and wireless communication systems across commercial and infrastructure projects.

Key Responsibilities:

•	Design and optimise DAS, small cell, and wireless communication systems
•	Conduct RF site surveys, path loss calculations, and signal testing
•	Perform PIM and swept frequency testing to resolve network issues
•	Install, configure, and optimise Nextivity Cel-Fi systems
•	Troubleshoot interference, signal leakage, and network performance issues
•	Prepare engineering documentation, commissioning reports, and as-built drawings
•	Ensure compliance with ACMA regulations and telecommunications standards
•	Collaborate with project teams and clients to deliver technical solutions
•	Research and recommend improvements to telecommunications technologies and systems

Required Skills and Qualifications:

•	Bachelor’s degree in Electronics Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field
•	Minimum of 3 years of relevant professional experience as an Electronics Engineer or related occupation
•	Strong knowledge of RF systems, DAS technologies, wireless communications, and telecommunications infrastructure
•	Experience with RF testing equipment, spectrum analysers, PIM testing, and network optimisation activities
•	Knowledge of Australian telecommunications standards, ACMA regulations, and engineering compliance requirements
•	Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical communication skills
•	Ability to work collaboratively with operational, engineering, and project delivery teams

From $80,000 to $90,000 per annum, plus superannuation, depending on skills and experience.

About the role
We're looking for a Computer Network and Systems Engineer to plan, deploy and commission network infrastructure across enterprise and hyperscale data centre environments. You'll work hands-on with switching, routing and optical transport hardware, take ownership of Layer 2/3 network design and implementation, and support our clients through installation, testing, migration and troubleshooting on live projects.

Key responsibilities
Analysing customer requirements, technical documentation, network designs and complex system architecture specifications to determine appropriate implementation methods and infrastructure solutions, including the development, configuration and integration of computer systems.
Planning, deploying and commissioning enterprise network infrastructure within enterprise and hyperscale data centre environments.
Installing, configuring, integrating, testing and maintaining network hardware and infrastructure, including Ethernet switches, routers, optical transport equipment, servers, workstations and associated software and database applications.
Designing and configuring FreeBSD and OpenBSD systems in support of network and infrastructure requirements.
Implementing Layer 2 and Layer 3 network connectivity, including VLAN configuration, IP addressing, routing and network integration in accordance with project and customer requirements.
Performing network testing, fault diagnosis and troubleshooting, including the use of specialised test equipment and software, to identify and resolve network infrastructure, connectivity and performance issues, and providing specialist support for network problems and emergencies.
Executing network migrations, equipment replacements and infrastructure upgrades while minimising disruption to production services.
Researching, evaluating and monitoring network infrastructure, traffic, activity, capacity and usage to ensure networks continue to operate at optimal performance and integrity, and assessing and recommending improvements to network operations and integrated hardware, software, communications and operating systems.
Providing network programming in support of specific business needs and requirements.
Working closely with project managers, customer representatives, vendors and other engineering teams to coordinate project implementation activities and ensure successful project delivery.
Preparing and maintaining technical documentation, installation records, network inventory, test results and as-built documentation, and recording the diagnosis and resolution of network faults, enhancements and modifications to networks, in accordance with company procedures and customer standards.
Ensuring that all installation, commissioning and maintenance activities comply with applicable technical specifications, quality standards and workplace health and safety requirements.
Performing such other duties as the Employer may allocate from time to time.

What you'll bring:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Network Engineering or a related engineering discipline
Strong working knowledge of enterprise networking (switching, routing, VLANs, IP addressing)
Experience with FreeBSD and/or OpenBSD systems administration
Experience working in large scale data centres
Hand on experience with fibre, fibre termination and testing
Comfortable working on-site in data centre environments, including practical completion support
Strong documentation habits and clear communication with clients and internal teams

At Qantas, our teams come together to create new and unique experiences for our customers.
A fantastic opportunity to be part of a team that focuses on cutting-edge technology and quality engineering principles.
Full-time and permanent position based at our new Product Innovation Centre in Adelaide. 


Join Qantas in our brand-new Product Innovation Centre located in Adelaide to help us ensure consumer needs are met by embedding robust testing strategies and automation practices that uphold software reliability, performance, and security. Deliver seamless, high-quality digital experiences that build customer trust and satisfaction.



As a Senior Quality Engineer – Conversational AI, you’ll be responsible for testing and validating chatbot solutions while helping shape and evolve our CAI quality engineering capability. You’ll work closely with product, engineering and AI teams to design automated chatbot tests, validate conversation flows, and troubleshoot issues as they arise. With the freedom to identify and implement the best solutions, you’ll continuously improve our tools, frameworks and overall approach to CAI testing.



You’ll Have

Strong experience in Quality Engineering or QA, with hands-on experience testing Conversational AI or chatbot platforms
Proven experience using Cyara Botium for chatbot test automation
Expertise in testing conversation flows, intents, entities and dialogue management across multiple scenarios
Experience validating chatbot integrations with backend systems and APIs
Ability to design and execute end-to-end test strategies for AI-driven customer experiences
Experience embedding chatbot testing into CI/CD pipelines
Strong understanding of the challenges of testing AI systems, including ambiguity, edge cases and training data validation
Experience testing non-functional requirements such as performance, security and accessibility in conversational interfaces
Confidence collaborating with cross-functional teams to embed quality early in the delivery lifecycle
Strong analytical skills to interpret chatbot behaviour and translate insights into quality improvements
Excellent communication, documentation and stakeholder engagement skills
Experience working with Mobile apps as the entry point to the chat bot.
A continuous improvement mindset and passion for emerging AI technologies
Confidence contributing to go/no-go decisions for chatbot and CAI releases


Why Qantas?

At Qantas, your career can take you further than you imagined. You’ll join a team where creativity and passion drives success. Together we dream big and deliver even bigger. 

You’ll find diverse opportunities to grow, personally and professionally. From day one, you’ll be supported with hands-on training, coaching, and formal learning programs designed to help you excel. Your development is our priority because we know that when you thrive, so do our customers. 

And while this role is your starting point at Qantas, it’s just the beginning. We have a proud history of helping our people explore new paths and reach new heights - the destinations are endless. 


The Qantas employee benefits program offers amazing benefits that extend well beyond travel.  

We love to travel: Enjoy heavily discounted air travel within Australia and across the globe, both for you and your family and friends, as well as exclusive deals on accommodation and holidays.
We have flexible leave options: Make use of leave and flexible working opportunities including 18 weeks paid parental leave and the option to purchase additional paid leave for eligible employees.
We’ll give you access to thousands of rewards: Through our partnerships we can offer you discounts across shopping, food and wine, insurance, health and wellbeing, leisure and entertainment. You can also take advantage of our salary packaging program including motor vehicles, eligible portable electronic devices and professional memberships.
We’ll support your wellbeing: Whether it’s learning to better support your own and others’ mental health, our interactive wellbeing app or your very own tailored nutrition plan. 

Apply at the earliest to be considered!

Qantas is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing a working environment that embraces and values diversity and inclusion. By coming to work for us, you’ll be part of an organisation that encourages diversity, supports charities and environmental initiatives. We encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, and people of all backgrounds to apply. If you have any support or access requirements, we encourage you to advise us at time of application. Your personal information will be kept confidential in compliance with relevant privacy legislation.
